evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明; 異體字研訂說明
evidence.text: The dictionary reports that Shuowen’s headform for 票 was 𤐫, glossed “fire flying,” and analyzes it as fire plus a second graphic element. It says the lower 火 changed to 示 through clerical transformation, and that the modern form was later written 票. Its variant note calls 𤐫 the original form of 票. This supports an older graphic form and a clerical change, not the dossier’s altar/offering interpretation.
evidence.title: [A02895] 票 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry records older verb/adjective senses including rising fire, shaking, light rising or moving, and nimble/rapid; it cites Han shu passages for shaking and light movement, with Tang commentator Yan Shigu explaining 票然 as light movement. It separately lists paper money and written or printed documents serving as credentials, with examples from Qing and later works. This lexical list supplies examples but does not prove a direct semantic chain from flame to tickets.

evidence.text: The linked 𤐫 entry reports Shuowen’s analysis as 火 plus a form represented in the dictionary’s glyph font, quotes Guangyun’s statement that the old graph means “fire flying” and that it is now written 票, and cites Zhengzitong on 票 being written originally as that old form. This is evidence for a documented graphic succession; it does not independently confirm a two-pair-of-hands interpretation or “sparks” narrative.

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 形義通解; 字形資料
evidence.text: The account, citing He Linyi, describes the older form as 𤐫 with an upper [𦥑囟] element and lower 火; it says the upper part was reduced to 覀 and 火 was confused with 示, yielding the clerical form behind modern 票. It gives fire rising as the basic meaning, followed by light rising/wafting and rapid movement. Its displayed graph inventory has a seal form and bamboo-slip examples, but no oracle-bone or bronze examples; this is not evidence that no earlier forms existed.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 票

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.text: The entry cites Shuihudi Qin 日書甲種 slip 57 for 票風, interpreted as “strong/rapid wind,” and Han shu uses for 票然 and 票姚 with rapid or light movement senses. These are lexical examples distinct from graphic development. The Qin-slip use is reported by this dictionary; another scholarly discussion disputes a different Shuihudi 日書 reading 票行, so that disputed item should not be treated as secure corroboration.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 票

evidence.source: 葛希谷, Fudan University Center for Excavated Texts and Paleography
evidence.field: 論證：睡虎地秦墓竹簡《日書》甲種《盜者》篇“票行”
evidence.text: The author reports competing readings for a Shuihudi slip phrase 票行: earlier editors read it as 剽行 (“swift movement”), while another scholar proposes 膘胻; the author argues 票 should instead be read 少, supported by a parallel Han-period slip and phonetic loan examples. This disagreement concerns interpretation of that passage, not whether 票 can independently occur as a sound-bearing graph elsewhere.
evidence.title: 葛希谷：也說睡虎地秦墓竹簡《日書》甲種《盜者》篇的“票行”

search_audit.outcome: Inspected Qin-slip transcription and Fudan scholarship on a disputed Qin-slip reading. The checked 金布律 passage did not contain 票; no Qin/Han ticket or paper-token attestation was established.

The Unicode GetUnihanData endpoint returned an internal fetch error for both attempted URL forms. Ctext search result was available but its page returned 403 on open. Inspected Academia Sinica and official Taiwan CNS character records for readings and gloss metadata.

gaps: No securely verified oracle-bone or bronze attestation for 票/𤐫 was found in inspected materials; the CUHK entry’s displayed inventory includes seal and bamboo-slip examples but not oracle or bronze examples.

The interpretation of the upper component [𦥑囟] as a particular object or action is not independently established by the inspected primary pages. The dossier’s paired-hands/bag/basket and sparks account is not substantiated here; Shuowen’s phrase “with fire” and the later graphic resemblance to 覀/示 should not be elaborated into a concrete depicted object without stronger paleographic evidence.
No source inspected established a phonetic component in 票. Current readings and the supplied MC/OC row are reported separately and do not show that 覀 or another component was phonetic.

The documented old gloss is fire flying/rising. Light movement and rapidity have classical citations, including Han shu and a Qin-slip example as transmitted by CUHK, but the specific semantic bridge from leaping flame to movement is not directly demonstrated.

A secure early attestation for 票 meaning a paper slip, credential, ticket, or ballot was not located. The MOE dictionary provides examples for credentials and paper money in Qing-era and later texts; do not infer chronology solely from dictionary ordering.
The Unicode Unihan record could not be opened, and no official Unicode character-specific page was verified. The local kMandarin and Baxter–Sagart rows remain locally supplied evidence only.
No extract reuse assessment was made; the sources were used for character-specific paraphrase only.
